opportunities.title: 2027 C.L.R. James Research Fellowship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Research fellowship open to graduate students past qualifying exams, independent scholars and faculty of any nationality who are AAIHS members.
opportunities.description:
The C.L.R. James Research Fellowship is a small research award from the African American Intellectual History Society (AAIHS) for scholars working on Black intellectual history. Its purpose is to help a recipient move a dissertation towards completion or bring a book project closer to publication, and the deadline for the 2027 round was pushed back to 15 November 2026.

Two fellowships are offered. The money is meant mainly for research travel, either within the recipient's own country or abroad, but it can also go towards other research costs such as buying books or obtaining archival files. Winners are announced at the AAIHS annual conference and must spend the award by the end of December 2027, then send the society a detailed report on how it was used.

The award is open to graduate students who have passed their qualifying examinations, to independent scholars and to faculty members at any rank, with no nationality limit. That makes it a realistic option for African doctoral students and researchers whose projects deal with the history of Black thought, provided they join AAIHS before applying.
opportunities.benefits: Two awards of US$2,000 each. The funds are intended for domestic or international research travel, and may also be used for other research expenses such as books or copies of archival files.
requirements: Current member of AAIHS (sitting board members cannot apply)
Graduate students must already have passed their qualifying exams
Independent scholars and faculty of any rank are also eligible
Project aimed at finishing a dissertation or publishing a book
Open to applicants of any nationality
documents: One PDF combining a short CV (no more than 3 pages), a project proposal of 3 to 5 double-spaced pages and a budget
One letter of recommendation, sent by email as a Word or PDF attachment
opportunities.selection_process: An AAIHS awards committee reviews the proposals and chooses two fellows. The page does not publish detailed scoring criteria.
important_dates: Winners announced: at the AAIHS conference
Funds must be spent by: 30 December 2027
opportunities.about_provider: The African American Intellectual History Society is a scholarly association that promotes research and teaching on Black thought and culture in the United States and across the African diaspora. It runs an annual conference, publishes the Black Perspectives blog and offers small grants and prizes to researchers.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Put the CV, proposal and budget together in one PDF and email it to awards@aaihs.org before the deadline. Ask your referee to email the recommendation letter separately as an attachment. Questions can be sent to the same address.
opportunities.notes: Recipients must file a detailed report after using the funds. Membership of AAIHS is a condition, so join before you submit.

opportunities.title: CIMPA Fellowship: Learning over Structured High-Dimensional Objects (Bernoulli Center, EPFL, 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: CIMPA fellowship for young mathematicians based in a developing country, with travel up to EUR 1,600, accommodation at the Bernoulli Center and EUR 250 per week.
opportunities.description:
CIMPA is offering fellowships for young mathematicians from developing countries to join a six-week thematic research programme on learning over structured high-dimensional objects, covering the theory and complexity of these problems. The programme takes place at the Bernoulli Center in Lausanne, Switzerland, from 15 March to 23 April 2027 and is organised by Fiona Skerman and Anda Skeja of Uppsala University.

The stay combines two workshops with a PhD-level course, seminars, reading groups and working sessions, so fellows both learn and do research alongside the international participants. Attendance is free of charge, and the programme is aimed at people with at least a master's-level background.

For African mathematicians and early-career researchers this is a funded way to spend six weeks at a leading European research centre: CIMPA pays travel, accommodation and a weekly allowance for up to two laureates on this programme.
opportunities.benefits: Return travel of up to €1,600 (visa costs included), accommodation at the Bernoulli Center, and an allowance of €250 per week. Up to two fellows are funded for this programme. There is no participation fee.
requirements: Based in a developing country according to the IMU classification
Aged 36 or under, or PhD obtained within the last 5 years
At least Master 2 level
Must attend the full six weeks (never less than two thirds of the programme)
documents: Up-to-date CV covering scientific training, master's courses with their detailed content, thesis topic or publications with links
Motivation letter specific to this programme
Up to two recommendation letters, requested directly from referees through the system
Research project, only if the call asks for one
opportunities.selection_process: The programme organisers examine the applications. Candidates are told the outcome by letter in the weeks after the deadline.
opportunities.about_provider: CIMPA (Centre International de Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées) is an organisation that supports mathematical research and training in developing countries. Its fellowships send young mathematicians from those countries to thematic programmes at research centres in Europe.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account and apply on the CIMPA applications platform (applications.cimpa.info), which redirects to the submission site. Upload your CV and motivation letter and enter your referees so they can send letters directly.
opportunities.notes: CIMPA advises applying well before the deadline and asking referees early. Generic motivation letters are discouraged.

opportunities.title: EPFL Life Sciences Summer Research Program 2027
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Summer research programme for international students, including Africans, with financial support and eligible travel reimbursement.
opportunities.description:
The EPFL School of Life Sciences Summer Research Program places international bachelor's and first-year master's students in a research laboratory at EPFL in Lausanne, Switzerland, for eight weeks of hands-on lab work. The 2027 edition runs from 5 July to 27 August 2027, with 35 participating labs listed (a few of them based in Geneva).

Participants join a lab group and work on a research project in areas such as biology, biophysics, chemistry, bioengineering, bioinformatics and quantitative biology. The programme is designed for strong students who are considering a career in the life sciences and want real research experience at one of Europe's top technical universities.

African students enrolled in a life-science degree with top grades can apply; the programme is open internationally and the application is entirely online.
opportunities.benefits: Eight weeks of supervised research in an EPFL life-sciences laboratory. The programme page does not state the financial package.
requirements: Currently enrolled in a life-science degree (biology, biophysics, chemistry, bioengineering, bioinformatics, quantitative biology, genetics, medicine or similar)
GPA of 3.75/4.0 or equivalent, or in the top 5% of the class
At least two years of undergraduate study completed (up to first-year master's) before the start
Strong interest in a life-science career; basic life-science knowledge essential, lab experience a plus
documents: Online application form with GPA and short personal and scientific essays
Bachelor's transcript (and master's transcript if started) or official list of courses and grades
One recommendation letter
opportunities.selection_process: Only complete applications are reviewed. Selection looks at academic record, life-science understanding, essays and lab choices, with prior lab experience counting in the applicant's favour. Results are emailed about six weeks after the deadline.
important_dates: Results: about six weeks after the deadline
opportunities.about_provider: EPFL (École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne) is a leading Swiss public university of science and technology. Its School of Life Sciences hosts research groups in biology, neuroscience, bioengineering and related fields.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Read the programme site and FAQs, then complete the online form on EPFL's recruiting portal (programs-recruiting.epfl.ch). The form cannot be saved, so prepare essays, lab preferences, transcripts and your referee's details before you start.
opportunities.notes: The application must be finished in one sitting. The essay questions are published in the FAQs so you can draft them in advance.

opportunities.description:
The Chien-Tien Hsu Fellowship is offered by FIGO, the International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics, around its 2027 World Congress in Montréal, Canada (31 October to 5 November 2027). It supports up to two obstetrician-gynaecologists who are starting out in gynaecological oncology.

Each fellow spends five days on a clinical or academic placement in Canada before the congress and then attends FIGO Montréal 2027. The fellowship comes with a grant towards travel and other costs. FIGO's general congress bursaries for 2027 have already closed, but this fellowship remained open until 15 November 2026.

Young African gynaecologists with research in gynaecological oncology and an accepted congress abstract are well placed to apply, since the award is international and aimed at early-career specialists.
opportunities.benefits: A grant of US$5,000 for travel and other expenses, a five-day placement in Canada before the congress, and attendance at FIGO Montréal 2027.
requirements: Aged 40 or younger
Fluent in English
Postgraduate degree in obstetrics and gynaecology
Currently engaged in a research project in gynaecological oncology
Abstract accepted for FIGO Montréal 2027
opportunities.about_provider: FIGO is the global federation of national obstetrics and gynaecology societies. It works to improve women's health and rights worldwide and holds a World Congress every few years, with bursaries to reduce financial barriers to attendance.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the application link on FIGO's congress bursaries and fellowship page. An accepted abstract for the congress is required, so make sure your abstract has been submitted through the congress portal.
opportunities.notes: The general FIGO 2027 bursaries (US$1,000) are closed; only the Chien-Tien Hsu Fellowship remained open. Up to two fellows are chosen.

opportunities.title: Harvard LEAD Fellowship for Promoting Women in Global Health 2027-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Women global health leaders based in a low- or middle-income country with a master's or medical degree and 10+ years of experience can apply for a residential fellowship in Boston.
opportunities.description:
The Harvard LEAD Fellowship (Learn, Engage, Advance, Disrupt) is a one-year leadership programme run by the Harvard Global Health Institute with the Department of Global Health and Population at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health. It is meant for senior global health professionals in low- and middle-income countries who will mentor the next generation of women leaders in the field.

The 2027-2028 cohort runs from 1 September 2027 to 31 August 2028. Most of the year is virtual, with a six-week residency in Cambridge, Massachusetts, in April 2028. Fellows receive one-to-one executive coaching, faculty mentorship, an executive education course, leadership masterclasses and speaking opportunities. So far 26 fellows from 21 countries have taken part.

African professionals with a master's or medical degree and a decade of global health work are a natural fit, as the fellowship requires applicants to be based in an LMIC and to return there afterwards.
opportunities.benefits: The six-week residency is fully funded: visa fees, housing, return flights to Cambridge, course fees, a daily per diem and a logistics stipend. Coaching, mentorship and masterclasses are included throughout the year.
requirements: Master's or higher degree (MPH, MSc, MPA, MBA, PhD, DrPH, etc.) or a medical degree (MD, MBBS or equivalent); a bachelor's alone does not qualify
At least 10 years of full-time professional experience in global health (study time does not count)
Currently based or working in a low- or middle-income country and planning to return there
Full employer support, including six weeks' leave in April 2028
Valid passport and able to obtain a J-1 visa
No full-time fellowship of 4 months or more in the two years before arrival
documents: CV or résumé
Letter of intent (maximum 1.5 pages)
Four essays of up to 2,000 characters each: career development plan, project plan, mentoring plan, and expected impact
Letter of institutional commitment from the home institution
Letter of mentor commitment
Two further reference letters, at least one from the current or most recent employer
important_dates: Residency in Cambridge: six weeks in April 2028
opportunities.about_provider: The Harvard Global Health Institute is Harvard University's hub for cross-school work on global health challenges. It partners with the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health to run fellowships and training for health leaders.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the Reviewr portal linked from the fellowship page, uploading the essays, letter of intent and CV and arranging the commitment and reference letters. Questions go to HGHI_Fellowships@harvard.edu.
opportunities.notes: Work experience cannot replace the required postgraduate degree. The J-1 visa is not guaranteed by Harvard.

opportunities.title: ICTP 23rd International Workshop on Computational Physics and Materials Science: Total Energy and Force Methods (Jan 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: General applications for the ICTP Total Energy workshop in Trieste (13-15 January 2027) close 15 November 2026; the deadline for financial or visa support was 11 October 2026 and has passed, and there is no registration fee.
opportunities.description:
ICTP's 23rd International Workshop on Computational Physics and Materials Science, focused on total energy and force methods, takes place in Trieste, Italy, from 13 to 15 January 2027. The series has been held every two years since the 1980s and is one of the main meeting points for the electronic-structure community.

The programme covers new energy functionals, time-dependent phenomena, machine-learning methods and quantum computing for materials, among other topics, and includes poster sessions and the Walter Kohn Prize ceremony. It is co-sponsored by CECAM and Psi-k.

There is no registration fee, and a limited number of grants are available with priority for participants from developing countries, which makes the workshop accessible to African physicists and materials scientists.
opportunities.benefits: No registration fee. A limited number of grants for selected participants, with priority for those from developing countries (amounts not stated).

Grant priority for participants from developing countries
Poster abstract prepared on the ICTP template

Poster abstract using the ICTP template

opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply on the ICTP e-applications portal (activity smr 4335) and upload a poster abstract on the ICTP template. Contact smr4335@ictp.it with questions.

opportunities.description:

It is linked to the International Master Course in Physics of Complex Systems and supported by Politecnico di Torino and Capital Fund Management.

The college consists of four courses of nine lectures each, every one ending with an exam. Lecturers include Raffaella Burioni, Nicolas Macris, Kirone Mallick and Izaak Neri, among others. Participants who attend at least 80% of the lectures receive a certificate.

The school is open to qualified master's and PhD students and young researchers, with no registration fee and grants that give priority to participants from developing countries, so African students in physics, mathematics or related fields can apply.

opportunities.title: Joint ICTP-CCG Catalyst Facility Academic Writing Residency for Global South Scholars (Mar 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers who are nationals of, and affiliated with an institution in, an ODA-eligible country (priority to least developed countries) and have a completed draft paper can apply by 15 November 2026 for the 1-19 March 2027 residency in Trieste; limited grants cover airfare, accommodation and subsistence.
opportunities.description:
ICTP and the Climate Compatible Growth (CCG) programme are holding their second Academic Writing Residency for Global South scholars in Trieste, Italy, from 1 to 19 March 2027. The three-week residency helps researchers turn an almost finished paper on climate-compatible growth into a publishable article, with protected writing time and mentoring from experienced academics.

The research behind the paper must already be complete, since no new analysis is done during the stay. Themes include energy, transport, finance, governance, critical minerals, circularity and green hydrogen. The expected result is a preprint and, ideally, a journal submission, with possible support for open-access fees.

The residency is reserved for nationals of ODA-eligible countries working at universities or research institutes there, with priority for least developed countries, so it is squarely aimed at researchers from Africa and other developing regions.
opportunities.benefits: Return airfare, accommodation at the ICTP guesthouse, a daily subsistence allowance, in-person mentoring, and optional support for journal submission and open-access fees (subject to approval). There is no registration fee; a limited number of grants are available.
requirements: National of an ODA-eligible country (priority for least developed countries)
Affiliated with a university or research institution in an ODA-eligible country
A completed draft paper with all analysis finished
Topic aligned with one or more CCG research communities
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are judged on the quality and originality of the paper, its relevance to CCG themes, the applicant's academic profile and publications, co-authorship across institutions (especially South-South), and the potential for publication and impact.
opportunities.about_provider: The Abdus Salam International Centre for Theoretical Physics (ICTP) in Trieste is a UNESCO Category 1 institute governed by UNESCO, the IAEA and Italy that supports science in developing countries. Climate Compatible Growth is a research programme involving Loughborough University and Imperial College London that supports low-carbon development planning.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through the ICTP e-applications portal (activity smr 4340) and use the abstract template provided on the event page. Contacting CCG academics before applying is encouraged.
opportunities.notes: Co-authored papers and prior involvement in CCG capacity-building are viewed favourably. Contact: smr4340@ictp.it.

opportunities.title: Medical Humanities in the Anthropocene: Indo-Canadian Perspectives (international conference)
opportunities.provider: Centre for Canadian Studies, Jadavpur University
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Researchers can submit abstracts for this 3-4 February 2027 conference on medical humanities, Indigeneity, borders and justice.
opportunities.description:
The Centre for Canadian Studies at Jadavpur University in Kolkata, India, is marking its 20th anniversary with an international conference on medical humanities in the Anthropocene, looking at Indigeneity, borders and justice from Indian and Canadian perspectives. It takes place on 3 and 4 February 2027.

The call invites papers and posters on topics such as critical medical humanities, Indigenous healing, migration and health, and environmental humanities. Faculty and researchers submit abstracts of 500 to 700 words, while undergraduate students may present posters. Overseas participants may be allowed to present online, depending on logistics.

Two student prizes, the Victor Ramraj Memorial Prize and the Renate Eigenbrod Memorial Prize, are open to fourth-year BA, master's and PhD students. African researchers working on health, migration or Indigenous studies can take part at a modest fee.
opportunities.benefits: A chance to present research, with two student prizes for outstanding papers. Registration fees include lunch, refreshments and a conference kit; foreign delegates pay US$50 plus 18% GST (US$59).
requirements: Faculty, researchers and independent scholars: abstract of 500 to 700 words with a 50-word bio
Undergraduate students: poster only, abstract of 300 to 400 words
Prize applicants: current BA fourth-year, master's or PhD students, single authors, not prize winners in the last three years
Selected participants must pay the registration fee
documents: Abstract and short bionote
Full paper by 4 January 2027 if shortlisted for a prize
Payment receipt with transaction ID and contact details after acceptance
opportunities.selection_process: The organising committee reviews abstracts and sends acceptance notices. Prizes are awarded only if the committee judges a paper original and excellent; shortlisted students must present in person.
opportunities.about_provider: Jadavpur University is a public university in Kolkata, India. Its Centre for Canadian Studies promotes research on Canada, including Indigenous and diaspora studies, and is celebrating its 20th year.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Email your abstract and bionote to ccsju@jadavpuruniversity.in, stating whether you are entering for a prize. The registration link is sent only after acceptance.
opportunities.notes: Participants arrange their own accommodation. Online presentation is possible only for overseas participants.

opportunities.title: OIST Fully Funded PhD Program (2027 entry)
opportunities.provider: Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Fully funded five-year PhD in science and technology at OIST in Okinawa, open to applicants worldwide.
opportunities.description:
The Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology (OIST) Graduate University in Japan runs a fully funded five-year PhD programme in English that starts with laboratory rotations before students choose a thesis lab. OIST has no departments, so students can work across disciplines in the natural sciences, mathematics and engineering.

The 2027 admission round accepted applications from 31 July to 15 November 2026 (23:59 Japan time). Shortlisted candidates take part in a compulsory online Admissions Workshop with interviews between 18 January and 7 February 2027, and final results come out in mid-February 2027. Successful applicants can start on 1 May 2027, 1 September 2027 or 1 January 2028.

OIST admits around 60 graduate students a year from all over the world, with no nationality limit and no minimum English score, which makes it a strong option for African graduates seeking a funded PhD in Asia.
opportunities.benefits: A fully funded five-year PhD with what OIST describes as a comprehensive financial package. The application fee is 5,000 JPY (non-refundable).
requirements: Bachelor's or master's degree, or expected to finish one before enrolment
TOEFL iBT or IELTS from the last two years only if the qualifying degree was not taught in English (no minimum score)
GRE optional

Statement of purpose, up to 800 words
CV
2 to 5 recommendation letters in English from professorial-level faculty
English test score if required
Passport photo page
ID photo taken in the last 3 months
opportunities.selection_process: There is no written exam. Shortlisted applicants must attend an online Admissions Workshop with interviews. Supervisor availability matters, so a strong applicant can still be turned down if there is no space in their field.
important_dates: Admissions Workshop interviews: 18 January to 7 February 2027
Start options: 1 May 2027, 1 September 2027 or 1 January 2028
opportunities.about_provider: OIST is a graduate university in Okinawa, Japan, built around interdisciplinary research and a department-free structure. It teaches entirely in English and recruits faculty and students internationally.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Create an account on the OIST graduate school application site (graduateschool.oist.jp/apply) and upload all documents in English. You can submit only after at least two recommendation letters have arrived.
opportunities.notes: Check the faculty list and PhD supervision availability before applying. Lab members and postdocs cannot act as referees.

opportunities.title: Cancer Genomic Epidemiology (course bursary, Mar 2027)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Bursaries are available for researchers and clinicians attending this course at the Wellcome Genome Campus, 15-18 March 2027.
opportunities.description:
Wellcome Connecting Science is running a four-day residential course on cancer genomic epidemiology, subtitled Understanding Mutational Signatures of Cancer to Inform Prevention, at the Wellcome Genome Campus in Hinxton, near Cambridge, UK, from 15 to 18 March 2027. It is organised with the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) of the WHO and the Wellcome Sanger Institute.

The course is for early and mid-career scientists in genomics, epidemiology, clinical or public health who want to learn how mutational signatures in tumour genomes can reveal causes of cancer and guide prevention. Places are limited and awarded on merit, with preference for applicants working on related projects.

The course fee covers accommodation and meals, and merit-based bursaries can halve the fee, which helps African researchers in cancer epidemiology attend. The organisers can also provide letters for UK visa applications.
opportunities.benefits: Course fee £810, including accommodation and all meals. Limited merit-based bursaries reduce the fee by up to 50%.

opportunities.description:
The Mahindra Humanities Center at Harvard University is offering four one-year postdoctoral fellowships for 2027-28 on the theme of environmental humanities. Scholars from any humanistic discipline can apply, as long as their research speaks to the environment, and fellows spend the year in residence in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

Fellows take part in a seminar that meets every two weeks across both semesters, alongside the Center's wider programme of lectures and events. International fellows hold the post from 1 September 2027 to 31 August 2028 on a J-1 research scholar visa or F-1 OPT. There is no nationality restriction, so recent African PhDs working on climate, land, water, extraction or ecological history are well placed to apply.
opportunities.benefits: Stipend of $70,000 for the year, medical insurance, $2,500 in research funds, and up to $1,500 for moving costs (only for fellows not already living in Greater Boston).

Research in a humanities discipline connected to environmental humanities
Able to be in residence at Harvard from September 2027 to August 2028
No nationality restriction
documents: CV
Research statement of 1,000 to 3,000 words
One writing sample of up to 40 pages
Three referees, who are asked for letters automatically after you submit
opportunities.about_provider: The Mahindra Humanities Center is Harvard's main hub for interdisciplinary work in the humanities. It runs seminars, lectures and fellowships that bring scholars from around the world to Harvard.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply through Harvard's ARIES academic positions portal (posting 16602), uploading the CV, research statement and writing sample and entering three referees. Referees are emailed automatically and must upload their letters by 4 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: Four fellowships are offered. Questions go to the Center's fellowship coordinator, Lisa Brown. The Center also runs Interdisciplinary Dissertation Completion Fellowships.

opportunities.description:
The A.S. Hornby Educational Trust, together with the University of Exeter's School of Education, funds up to ten experienced English language teachers from low- and middle-income countries to take the one-year MEd in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages (TESOL), starting in September 2027.

The scholarship is fully funded and is aimed at teachers who will return to strengthen English language teaching in their own countries. Most African countries are eligible as OECD DAC recipients, but Exeter cannot accept applicants from countries where the UK does not issue student visas, which currently includes Cameroon and Sudan. Applicants should be working teachers with at least three years of full-time experience.
opportunities.benefits: Full tuition fees, a monthly living stipend and return international travel for the one-year MEd TESOL.
requirements: Resident in and working in an OECD DAC least developed, low, lower-middle or upper-middle income country
Not from a country where the UK issues no student visas (Afghanistan, Cameroon, Myanmar, Sudan are excluded)
At least 3 years of full-time TESOL or related teaching experience after the first degree
Undergraduate degree equivalent to a UK upper second class or better
Not already holding a doctorate or a UK master's in TESOL, applied linguistics, English or a related field
No language test needed to apply, but English proficiency must be stated

Supporting documents only if shortlisted
opportunities.selection_process: Applications are shortlisted on the online form, shortlisted candidates are interviewed between 15 and 24 February 2027, and final decisions follow by early March.
opportunities.about_provider: The A.S. Hornby Educational Trust supports English language teaching around the world, building on the legacy of the lexicographer A.S. Hornby. The University of Exeter is a research-intensive UK university whose School of Education is well known for TESOL.

opportunities.description:
Peking University (PKU) is accepting applications from international students for full-time master's and doctoral programmes starting in September 2027, and applicants can be considered for several scholarships at the same time. These include the PKU Scholarship for New International Students, the Chinese Government Scholarship (Type B, university programme) and the Beijing Government Scholarship.

Admission follows an 'application plus examination' model: the International Student Division checks the file, then each school's expert panel reviews it and runs a second-round assessment between January and March 2027. Programmes are offered in Chinese and in English across PKU's campuses in Beijing and its Shenzhen Graduate School.

For African graduates, this is a route to one of China's top two universities with funding that can cover tuition, housing, living costs and insurance. The first-round window runs until 25 December 2026, so documents such as authenticated degree certificates should be prepared early.
opportunities.benefits: Depending on the scheme: the Chinese Government Scholarship (Type B) offers full or partial cover of tuition, accommodation, living allowance and medical insurance; the PKU Scholarship for New International Students covers full or partial tuition, living expenses and medical insurance; the Beijing Government Scholarship (Types A, B, C) ranges from tuition and insurance up to tuition, housing, a living stipend and insurance. The page does not give amounts.
requirements: Non-Chinese citizen with a valid passport, in good health and with no criminal record
Master's: bachelor's degree recognised by China's Ministry of Education
PhD: master's degree (bachelor's holders may apply to some science and engineering PhDs)
Chinese-taught programmes: HSK level 6 with at least 200 (sciences) or 210 (humanities) and writing 65 or more
English-taught programmes: TOEFL, GRE (above 315) or other proof as each programme sets
Beijing Government Scholarship age limits: master's 35 or under, PhD 40 or under
documents: Degree certificates with CSCSE authentication
Academic transcripts
Personal statement and research plan (about 1,500 words for master's, 3,000 for PhD)
Resume and signed commitment letter
Two recommendation letters
Language test scores
Passport information pages
List of publications, if any
Any extra materials required by the school
opportunities.selection_process: The International Student Division first checks eligibility, then school expert panels review the files and hold a second-round assessment (January to March 2027) of research ability, language and potential. A preliminary admission list is released by the end of May 2027.
important_dates: Preliminary admission list: by end of May 2027
opportunities.about_provider: Peking University, founded in 1898, is one of China's leading comprehensive research universities. Its International Student Division handles admission and scholarships for degree-seeking international students.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply online through PKU's International Student Service System (studyatpku.com), choosing up to two programmes and paying the non-refundable RMB 800 fee per programme. Indicate the scholarships you wish to be considered for, upload all documents and submit before 25 December 2026.
opportunities.notes: Master's programmes last 2 to 3 years and PhDs 4 to 5 years. Beijing Government Scholarship holders cannot hold another Chinese government or PKU scholarship. Check each school's catalogue for language scores, as the general guide's TOEFL figure is unclear.

opportunities.description:
The Exeter Excellence Scholarships give international students a £15,000 discount on the first year of tuition for a taught master's degree at the University of Exeter in south-west England. Round 1 of the 2027/28 scheme is for September 2027 entry and offers 150 awards.

Most campus-based master's programmes across the university's three faculties are eligible, including computer science, economics, engineering, management, psychology, law and education. Postgraduate certificates and diplomas, degree apprenticeships, online programmes and a few named courses are excluded.

The scheme is aimed at self-funded international students, so African applicants paying their own fees can use it to bring down the cost of a UK master's considerably. You need a programme offer before applying for the scholarship.
opportunities.benefits: 150 awards of £15,000 off tuition fees in the first year (one-off, not renewed).
requirements: International fee status (including EU students paying international fees)
UK upper second-class (2:1) degree or equivalent
Conditional or unconditional offer for an eligible campus-based taught master's starting September 2027
Self-funded
Not combined with other Exeter scholarships
documents: Online scholarship webform
Personal statement of up to 300 words answering two questions (150 words each) on your aspirations and on what you would contribute as an Exeter Scholar
opportunities.selection_process: Awards are made on academic merit as shown in your master's application, together with your ambitions, a clear plan, social responsibility and willingness to engage with the university community. Outcomes are sent by the end of 25 February 2027.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Exeter is a research-intensive UK university and member of the Russell Group, with campuses in Exeter and Cornwall. It is ranked 136th in the QS World University Rankings 2027, according to the university.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your master's programme first. Once you hold an offer, fill in the Round 1 scholarship webform linked from the award page. Questions go to admissions-scholarships@exeter.ac.uk.
opportunities.notes: The award page shows the deadline time as 'II:59 GMT', probably meaning 23:59. Later rounds may follow, but only Round 1 was published.

opportunities.description:
The University of Glasgow African Excellence Award is a merit scholarship for outstanding students from across Africa who want to take a one-year, full-time taught master's degree at Glasgow in Scotland. The 2027/28 round is for the September 2027 intake and covers almost every subject the university teaches.

The award takes the form of a 75% reduction in tuition fees, which in most colleges is worth more than £20,000. Up to 16 awards are available, and shortlisted applicants are invited to an interview.

Applicants must live in Africa and hold a passport from an African country, have grades equivalent to a UK first-class degree, and set out a clear career or development plan. You can apply for the award before you have an offer, but you need an offer to be considered for interview.
opportunities.benefits: A 75% tuition fee waiver for one year of study. Examples given by the university: about £20,543 off in Arts and Humanities, £25,281 in Medical, Veterinary and Life Sciences, £26,111 in Science and Engineering and the Adam Smith Business School, and £21,206 in Social Sciences. The actual value depends on the fee in your offer letter.
requirements: Domiciled in Africa and holding a passport from an African country
Grades equivalent to a UK first-class honours degree
Holding or applying for an offer for a one-year full-time taught master's starting September 2027
International fee status
Clear career and/or development plan
Must meet the UKVI living-cost requirement
documents: Online scholarship application form, including your career or development plan
Offer for an eligible master's programme (needed before interview)
opportunities.selection_process: Applicants are judged on academic excellence and their plans. Shortlisted candidates are invited to interview and contacted by 7 May 2027. Up to 16 awards are made.
opportunities.about_provider: The University of Glasgow, founded in 1451, is one of the oldest universities in the English-speaking world and a member of the UK's Russell Group of research-intensive universities.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for your master's programme at Glasgow, then complete the African Excellence Award form on the university's scholarship portal (linked from the award page). Questions go to student.recruitment@glasgow.ac.uk.
opportunities.notes: Postgraduate diplomas and certificates are not eligible. The award cannot be combined with other Glasgow scholarships or discounts except the alumni discount; if you are offered more than one award, the lower one is withdrawn.

opportunities.title: Nipissing University Guaranteed Entrance Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Secondary-school leavers, including international students, entering Nipissing with an average of 80% or more.
opportunities.description:
Nipissing University in North Bay, Ontario, gives guaranteed entrance scholarships to students who apply straight from secondary school, and international applicants are included. There is no separate application: every eligible new student is considered automatically on the basis of their admission average, for September or January entry.

The award is renewable, so a strong average can reduce tuition for the whole degree as long as the student keeps up their grades and course load. For African school-leavers comparing Canadian options, it is a predictable, merit-based discount rather than a competition.
opportunities.benefits: Based on the 2026-27 table: an average of 95% or more earns free tuition at the domestic rate (worth over $24,000 in total); 90-94% earns $2,500 a year; 85-89% earns $1,500 a year; 80-84% earns $1,000 a year.
requirements: Applying directly from secondary school for September or January entry
Canadian and international applicants are both considered
Admission average of at least 80%, based on the best six Grade 12 (4U/4M) courses or the IB score as of 30 June
Not in Consecutive Education, the Commerce/BBA college-partnership or Nursing Scholar Practitioner programmes
Renewal requires the set cumulative GPA and 24 credits each year
documents: None beyond the normal undergraduate admission application
opportunities.selection_process: Automatic: the award level is set by the admission average, with no separate application or competition.
opportunities.about_provider: Nipissing University is a public, primarily undergraduate university in North Bay, Ontario, known for small classes and its education and liberal arts programmes.
opportunities.how_to_apply: Apply for undergraduate admission to Nipissing as a secondary-school applicant; the scholarship is assessed automatically from your grades. January entrants must take 9 credits in the winter term, and their payment is deferred to September.
opportunities.notes: The official page gives no deadline; the listing's 13 and 20 November dates are not on it, so this entry is marked rolling. The amounts shown are from the 2026-27 table and may be updated for 2027 entry.
